now.note: The fourteen pages are built and waiting on your read against Florida practice.

phases.title: Foundation, home page and about page
phases.intro: Both pages exist in Spanish and in English, on the design system and the publishing rules the rest of the site will be built on.

items.name: Spanish first, English complete
items.desc: Every page in both languages, with a language switch in the bar, in the phone bar, and floating on the page.

items.name: The design system
items.desc: Palette, type scale, spacing and motion, set once so each new page is assembled rather than designed again.

items.name: The home page
items.desc: Opening frame, the firm's introduction, four featured practice areas, the television appearances, the Orlando office with a map, and the closing invitation.

items.name: The about page
items.desc: Your name and summary, the biography, and the record: admission, degrees and AILA membership.

items.name: Bar, footer and phone bar
items.desc: On a phone the bottom bar calls the office, opens WhatsApp, and switches language.

items.name: Every word traced to a source
items.desc: Nothing on the site was written for it. Each string comes from camimlaw.com, from Campos Muños Law's published pages, or from a checked record, and an automated check fails the build if one cannot be traced.

items.name: Ten checks that run before anything ships
items.desc: Colour contrast on every page in both languages, accessibility structure, sideways overflow from 320 to 1920 pixels, and the framing of the photographs.

items.name: A private preview
items.desc: A build that publishes only the reviewed pages, marked not to be indexed, so work in progress is never public.

phases.short: The rest of the site, and launch
phases.title: The rest of the site, and launch
phases.intro: The pages that turn two finished pages into a working firm website, and putting it live on camimlaw.com.

items.name: Fourteen practice-area pages
items.desc: Green card, family petitions, citizenship, deportation defence, asylum, VAWA, DACA, U and T visas, fiancé(e) visas, TPS, work permits, consular processing and special immigrant juvenile status.

items.name: The services index
items.desc: One page listing all fourteen, and the route into each.

items.name: Consultation page and intake form
items.desc: Name, phone, preferred language and topic, delivered to whichever inbox you name.

items.name: Payments page
items.desc: The existing LawPay link, presented as a page rather than a loose link.

items.name: The statements the Bar rules expect
items.desc: The admission limitation and the accompanying notices, in wording you or your counsel supply.

items.name: Search and existing links
items.desc: Sitemap, structured data, titles and descriptions, and a redirect from every old Squarespace address so links already out in the world keep working.

items.name: Launch on camimlaw.com
items.desc: Domain, hosting, certificates, and the switch itself.

phases.title: Video, reviews and conversation
phases.intro: The things the firm already owns that the current site does nothing with — eleven Spanish videos and a five-star review record — and the ways someone can start talking to the firm without filling in a form.

items.name: The eleven Spanish videos
items.desc: Hosting decided, poster frames, captions, and each video placed on the practice-area page it explains.

items.name: The broadcast segments
items.desc: Telemundo, Univision and TVV made playable where the footage allows, rather than stills.

items.name: Transcripts
items.desc: Each video's Spanish transcript on the page, readable for anyone who cannot play sound and the part search engines can actually read.

items.name: Google reviews on the site
items.desc: The live rating and a selection of reviews, updating on their own rather than being retyped.

items.name: Live chat, Spanish first
items.desc: A chat on the page that continues in WhatsApp, on the number the office already uses.

items.name: Instagram
items.desc: The firm's feed on the site, updating on its own.

phases.title: Measurement, review and handover
phases.intro: The pass over the finished site: what it measures, whether everything on it still holds, how it reads end to end, and everything needed to run it after I hand it over.

items.name: Analytics
items.desc: Which pages bring enquiries, which language they arrive in, and where people stop.

items.name: Search, after launch
items.desc: Search Console, what Google has actually indexed, and fixing what only a live site reveals.

items.name: The checks across every page
items.desc: The full suite run over the finished site, not just the pages it was written against: contrast, accessibility, sideways overflow, and the copy gate.

items.name: Every imported fact confirmed
items.desc: A pass over everything taken from Campos Muños Law's pages, checked against what you confirm holds in Florida.

items.name: A design review of the whole site
items.desc: Every page read end to end on a phone, a tablet and a desktop, with the rough edges fixed.

items.name: Handover
items.desc: How to edit a page, how to publish, and what to check when something looks wrong. Written down, and walked through once.
